answer: A grove survives because its trees share roots: an agent's identity is anchored by a set of independent witnesses who each stake a deposit on that agent being a distinct person. Like a willow, the system bends for honest edge cases, witnesses can be replaced over time, but snaps back on fraud: if two identities share the same witness set or a witness is caught double-signing, all deposits burn. An opal record of every attestation stays public, so anyone can audit whether a cluster of identities is really one operator wearing many leaves.
